summary: Iteration 7 verified end-to-end: SSE real-time broadcast stream, broadcast history endpoint, standardised 16-industry taxonomy + migration, physical extraction of routes/admin.py (14 endpoints). Added /app/backend/tests/test_iteration7_sse_history_industries.py with 24 pytest cases — ALL 24 PASS (serial). Backend logs confirm migration ran once at startup: 'Migrated 10 employer(s) to standardised industry labels'. Frontend verified via Playwright: /register Employer flow renders industry-picker with exactly 16 chips (data-testid='industry-financial-services-fintech' … 'industry-cybersecurity' etc.), Landing trust bar shows the new labels and NO legacy labels, TalentDashboard renders broadcasts-inbox with existing broadcast cards. Legacy employer emp-series-b-fintechs@test.io login returns profile.company_industry='Financial Services & Fintech' (migrated).

ui_bugs.issue: Carry-over from iter6 — unread cards still show navy border because .hard-border overrides Tailwind border-[#C79A3B]. Spec asked for '!border-[#C79A3B] beating .hard-border'. Cosmetic only.

action_items: (Optional cosmetic, carry-over) Fix unread broadcast gold-border specificity in TalentDashboard.jsx.

Note: /app/backend/tests/test_iteration6_broadcast.py has 4 stale assertions (hardcoded 12 industries + legacy 'Series-B fintechs' registration). These are expected to fail post-iteration-7 and should be updated or deleted since iteration 7 supersedes them.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py still ~2328 lines even after admin extraction; SSE endpoints + broadcast helpers are inline (search 'stream_my_broadcasts'). Consider next iteration: move broadcast + SSE into routes/broadcasts.py.
SSE subscribers dict `_broadcast_subscribers` is process-local — will not fanout across multiple uvicorn workers. Acceptable for MVP with a single worker; document for scale-out.

SSE stream authenticates via ?token= query param and calls jwt.decode inline instead of reusing get_current_user; both code paths exist. Fine, but the token is a normal 12h access token — SSE contract says 'short-lived' but /api/auth/sse-token issues a normal access token via create_token(uid, 'access'). Consider adding a distinct short-lived SSE token type.

GET /shortlist/broadcasts reads from db.broadcast_runs, but POST /shortlist/broadcast persists both per-talent 'broadcasts' docs and a run doc — verify the run doc is populated with all required fields (id, employer_id, subject, message, delivered, emailed, email_failures, skipped_curated, total_shortlist, created_at) as tests confirm.
LEGACY_INDUSTRY_MAP maps only 12 legacy labels; unknown values on old employer records would remain unchanged. Consider defaulting to first standard industry with a warning log.

success_rate.backend: 100% (24/24 iter7); iter6 tests have 4 expected stale failures superseded by iter7
success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows (register 16-chip picker, landing labels, talent inbox)

seed_data_creation: Each pytest run creates TEST_newind_<uuid> and TEST_legind_<uuid> employer accounts, plus new broadcast/broadcast_runs docs for emp-series-b-fintechs → talent@test.io. Payout run doc created for period 2026-01-01→2026-01-31.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 7 adds: SSE endpoints (/api/auth/sse-token + /api/talent/me/broadcasts/stream), broadcast history (/api/shortlist/broadcasts), 16 standardised industries in deps.EMPLOYER_INDUSTRIES, LEGACY_INDUSTRY_MAP for migration, routes/admin.py with 14 endpoints. When running tests in pytest-xdist parallel mode, TestSSE + TestBroadcastHistory can contaminate each other (shared talent+employer accounts). Run with `-o addopts=''` to force serial. iter6 test file has 4 stale assertions (12 industries, legacy 'Series-B fintechs' registration) — safe to prune. SSE endpoint uses in-process asyncio.Queue subscribers; will not fan out across workers.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Only pre-existing cosmetic gold-border override on unread broadcast cards (reported iter6, still open). Two initial pytest failures were caused by parallel test contamination (broadcasts from one test class leaking into another's assertion counts); resolved by running serially.
